headline: This law orders federal agencies to study whether a three-digit dialing code could be used for a national suicide and mental health crisis hotline, and to review how well the existing lifeline serves veterans.
what_it_does: The law directs the Federal Communications Commission to lead a study with the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration and the Department of Veterans Affairs. The study looks at whether a three-digit N11 phone code could be set aside for a national suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline. It also reviews how well the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline is working, including its service to veterans. The agencies must report their findings to specified congressional committees. The law does not provide any new money for this work.

who_it_affects.group: People who are having thoughts of suicide or a mental health crisis
who_it_affects.how: The study may lead to changes in how crisis hotlines are reached, but the law itself does not change how anyone calls for help today.
The Department of Veterans Affairs must review how well the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline and the Veterans Crisis Line meet veterans' needs.
The FCC must coordinate the feasibility study and report its results to Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on August 14, 2018, when it was enacted. The bill does not set a specific deadline for the reports in the summary provided.
